brief: c277, promoted. MK_NEED = [0, 4, 13] (line ~3369) is read in exactly one place — mkTrades(i), line ~3461 — and it decides how many of the three market stalls open. #184 measured the supply it is set against and the numbers are in the ledger: the store hands the market a MEDIAN 53.1 units against MK_CAP 18 over 51 markets, three stalls are open on 86% of them, and mkTotal is never 0 (minimum 0.7). The 4 and the 13 are therefore dead constants and 'a thin February market' is unreachable. Re-measure that distribution yourself first — #184's numbers are eight iterations old and the crate work has since drawn off the top of it — then set the thresholds against the supply the market ACTUALLY sees across a year, so a lean market opens two pitches and a fat one three, and the lane in late winter is visibly a smaller market than the lane in September.
successLooksLike: A histogram of mkTotal per market, 6 seeds x a year, with the open-stall count by season beside it; stalls-open is no longer 3 on 86% of markets, and the season it thins in is the season the allotments are bare. drawMarketOver's crate curve (0.67 spring / 1.87 winter / 5.33 summer / 11.44 autumn, #184) re-measured, since it is cut from the same mkUnits and will move with this.
avoid: Do not add a fourth stall — #184 already found the CROWD is the bound, not the shelf (0.72 browsers a market, median 0). Do not read a ratio: identical numbers at two settings is a DEAD constant and the supply was always the cap, so sweep the AXIS — the season — and not the constant, and pool six seeds. If the honest answer turns out to be that MK_NEED should be a function of the season rather than a fixed ladder, say so and build that; the deliverable is a market whose size tracks the year, not three numbers.
